Native qualification: R3-ME-008-D1: Shafaq’s November 23 account dates the blockade to Wednesday night and reopening to Thursday, corresponding to November 20–21, 2019. Baghdad Today independently published a reopening account early on November 21, after protesters withdrew from the gate. The border-authority interview relayed by Arab Times confirms a short interruption and resumed passenger and commercial movement in both directions, but does not independently supply its event date. The Wednesday-night to early-Thursday-morning chronology, reinforced by the official description of only a few hours, establishes a spell below 24 hours. Exact clocks remain unknown; crossing a calendar date does not make this a greater-than-24-hour closure. The linked Safwan sit-in’s own November 19 statements express solidarity with Baghdad protesters and opposition to political-party control and delay; these are attributed local demands, not proof that every nationwide protest demand motivated the gate blockade.
